_about: 카드별 그림 지시(영어). 카드 이름만으로 모습이 분명하지 않거나 꼭 들어가야 할 것이 있을 때 카드 ID로 적는다. 스페셜 · 유니크는 모두 적는다(새로 만들 때도). build_prompts.js가 프롬프트의 'Art direction' 줄로 넣는다.
SP-B1: A colossal being of living fire who swallowed the sleeping giant Dormak's heart-fire whole — one of a kind, not a goblin or any ordinary creature: a towering, majestic titan of cracked black basalt and flowing magma, taller than Fortan's chimneys and gun bastions, which look like toys at his feet. In his open chest Dormak's heart-fire blazes like a furnace sun behind ribs of cooling rock, and molten light pours from his eyes and mouth. One arm is raised and a cannon-blast of fire erupts from his palm — each breath he exhales is a whole battery's volley — while pillars of smoke and ash rise around his head like a crown. Tiny goblin gunners kneel on the bastion walls below, lit by his glow, not daring to speak his name. Behind him the volcano-chest of the giant Dormak splits open across the whole sky. Terrible grandeur, not a monster.
SP-B2: The heart is the focus: an enormous iron heart forged from the giant Sorgrim's sinew-ore — dark adamant plates, brass valves and pistons like arteries, molten forge-light pulsing through its seams — beating at the centre of the image, larger than a forge furnace. The one who swallowed it is a colossal armoured presence that is only partly seen: his vast shape is veiled in steam, shadow and forge smoke and revealed only in glimpses — the edge of a riveted iron shoulder like a cliff, a giant gauntleted hand resting on an anvil the size of a house, two eyes glowing high above in the darkness. Hundreds of chains and pipes run from the heart up into the hidden body; let the viewer imagine the full titan from these clues. Around it stretches the underground forge-cathedral of Durkheim; rows of golems, tiny by comparison, kneel facing the heart, their own chest-lights waking in rhythm with its beat, the oldest and most patched golem kneeling closest. He ascended without any god: instead of a halo, slowly turning rings of gears and golden runes circle the heart.
SP-B3: The Seventh: a gnome-built automaton prototype that one day began to think. An elegant copper-and-glass body with seven glowing lightning nodes (no numerals), a lightning brain visible inside a glass dome head, one hand raised in wonder at a spark it made itself. Tiny gnome scholars look up at it from its feet.
SP-G1: Karno Ashmane: a colossal duel-titan of living stone and ash, one of a kind — not an orc (no tusks, no green skin, no orc features). A towering warrior body of cracked dark granite and basalt with glowing ochre-orange magma seams, every one of his hundred duel scars a molten crack; a vast mane of grey ash and drifting embers streams from his head and shoulders like a volcanic plume (the 'ash mane'); fists like boulders bound in ancient leather straps; his face is a stern, noble mask of stone with burning eyes. He stands in a stone duel ring cracked into a crater, mid-stride and roaring a challenge, rock dust and embers exploding around his feet. Behind him the mountain-sized earth dragon Gorbas, forests on its back, lowers its great head to meet him eye to eye, as if for a hundred-and-first duel, while the standing stones and nomad camps of the Garun steppe lie tiny below and a trail of ash-grey smoke drifts across the plain behind him.
SP-G2: Lisiel Silvermoon, a walking forest that moves only on nights of the waxing moon — one of a kind, neither elf nor troll: a tall being half figure and half tree, bark skin threaded with silver moonlit veins, branches for hair, ember-scarred bark with young green leaves regrowing from every scar, saplings sprouting wherever it steps. It once took a burning forest's fire into its own body and raised a thousand-year forest from the ashes in a single night. Silver moonlight mixed with green spore-light; the forest dragon Verdan's branch-antlers form a canopy above.
SP-G3: She Who Lulls the Sea: the oldest song remembered by the water dragon Marencia, given a body — one of a kind, not a merfolk priestess. A serene woman-shaped being whose body from the waist down and through her flowing hair is living, translucent water; her hands are joined as she sings, and her song spreads over the dark sea as glowing rings of light; a blade passing through her becomes only ripples. Far below, in the black trench, the faint glow of the sleeping giant Talakus's colossal heart slows to the rhythm of her song. Behind her the translucent serpentine body of Marencia coils through the sky like a river of light, forming a halo. Calm, sacred and vast.
SP-A1: Azra the Shadowless at the height of her ascension — far grander than any demon blade-dancer: a colossal, regal figure standing above the sunless canyon city of Noctar, so tall that its violet-lit spires reach only to her knees. Her great curved horns form a dark crown framed by a total eclipse that serves as her halo; a vast cloak of living night spills from her shoulders down the canyon walls like a waterfall of shadow. Every shadow in the city — of towers, bridges and kneeling demons — stretches and bends toward her like supplicants, yet she herself casts none: the ground beneath her feet is bright and bare, make the missing shadow unmistakable. Her face is serene and half-veiled by drifting shadow-silk, eyes glowing violet. A burning contract scroll floats beside her open hand, its blood seal glowing. Above her in the sky the faceless shadow king Morkas holds his scales, one pan weighed down by something veiled — what she gave. Calm, still, overwhelming power — not an action pose.
SP-A2: The First Knight of Solante, the first ever to swear an oath to the Mother of Dawn — a mythic champion, not an ordinary knight: lifted by the goddess herself, vast wings of light bursting from his back, rising from one knee with his sword raised toward the dawn; where his blade is raised the night recoils and sunrise floods the sky.
SP-A3: Isaac who unravelled the stars, the first to read the star glyphs — a transcendent star-mage, not an ordinary elf or mage: he pulls threads of starlight down from the sky into an open book while a whole constellation unravels and re-weaves itself around him as abstract glyphs, and the sky obeys; silver hair and robes swept by star-wind.
SR-A1: The greatsword of Hargan the Judge, drawn only once to punish a god: a colossal two-handed sword of dark adamant and gold, scales of judgment engraved on the blade, standing point-down in a cracked divine altar under a beam of judgment light.
SR-A2: The bow of Seren the Gatekeeper, who guards the edge of the world: a tall bow of pale silver and starlight, a nocked arrow of light drawn by no hand, aimed at a dark horizon where the world ends.
SR-A3: The quill of Ivel the Recorder: a great feather quill whose ink is ether light, writing glowing abstract strokes in the air that turn into tiny real scenes; an endless library fades behind it.
UN-B1: An old goblin artillery captain of Fortan with a long grey ear-tuft and a brass spyglass, commanding a battery of cannons; even while falling he grins and holds a lit fuse.
UN-B2: Bron's first golem: an old, patched, riveted golem carefully building a new small golem from the parts of fallen comrades with gentle hands.
UN-B3: The gnome researcher who once bottled the lightning spirit Zrak, holding the biggest empty jar while cracked empty jars around her refill with lightning.
UN-G1: The great chief of the Rockfang tribe: an enormous orc with a stone-fang necklace, howling as his warband charges out of the dust behind him.
UN-G2: A moss troll keeper of thorns around the First Elder Tree; cut briars regrow from the roots all around him as he works.
UN-G3: A singer of the Spring Choir; her song spreads as glowing rings over the sea, and pale souls of the drowned ride the waves back toward the shore.
UN-A1: A demon writing his oath in his own blood with the edge of his blade; a crimson thread of the contract links his sword to his distant foe.
UN-A2: A radiant knight of Elad spreading her wings like a shield in front of her comrades, arrows breaking against the feathers.
UN-A3: A high-elf star-keeper atop Belumir's Needle, reading abstract star glyphs carried on the wind before the spells arrive.
UN-B1-7: A goblin gunner planting embers scooped from Talakus's black blood-pulse into his shells; behind him the struck ground keeps burning in long lines.
UN-B2-7: Two huge gate golems of Durkheim bound together by one massive steel chain, moving as one wall.
UN-B3-7: A walking tower wound with Keraun's lightning; its magnetic field bends the air — coins, dice and metal debris spin in orbit around it.
UN-G1-7: An orc plunder-king wielding weapons he took from fallen foes, a heap of captured arms and banners at his feet.
UN-G2-7: An old troll with seed pouches at his belt; wherever he walks after battle, a young forest springs up behind him.
UN-G3-7: A siren risen from Marencia's deep waters, singing on a rock; in the distance enemy soldiers turn their swords around against themselves.
UN-A1-7: A demon reaping souls with a great scythe; every soul he takes turns into a contract page fluttering into his hand.
UN-A2-7: A seraph priestess lifting the dawn light in both hands; fallen knights rise again behind her in the sunrise.
UN-A3-7: A high-elf devouring enemy spells: streams of foreign-coloured magic are pulled into his open palm and swallowed as light.
